comment.body: Thanks for confirming 0.102.3001. The behavior described is the documented lock-screen behavior: Awake can keep the computer awake, but Keep screen on applies only while unlocked. Windows may turn the display off on the lock screen according to its power settings, and Awake resumes its display request on unlock. See https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/powertoys/awake#lock-screen-behavior. The report does not yet show a failure while unlocked; the new version confirmation therefore does not identify a defect in the current contract.
